evidence.text:
• 
 Selling costs increased $63.9 million to $239.9 million in 2013 from $176.0 million in 2012 . This increase was primarily due to higher personnel and other costs incurred primarily for the continued expansion of our direct to consumer distribution channel. As a percentage of net revenues, selling costs increased to 10.3% in 2013 from 9.6% in 2012 .

attrs.management_says: SG&A increased $201M due to higher marketing, selling costs (direct-to-consumer expansion), product innovation/supply chain, and corporate services.
attrs.numbers_show: SG&A rose from $670.6M to $871.6M (E3, E15). Operating cash flow dropped from $199.8M to $120.1M (E6, E18) while net income rose $33.5M. The large cash outflows for selling ($63.9M increase, E40) and marketing ($41.1M increase, E39) directly reduce CFO, and the receivables increase of $34.5M (E7, E19) also consumed cash. The pattern fits the described investment in growth.

attrs.management_says: No explicit explanation provided in the evidence pack for the decline in operating cash flow from $199.8M to $120.1M while net income rose from $128.8M to $162.3M.
attrs.numbers_show: CFO fell $79.7M (39.9%) despite a $33.5M rise in net income. SG&A increased $201M (largely cash expenses: marketing +$41M, selling +$64M, product innovation +$51M, corporate +$45M). Current assets rose $225M (receivables +$34.5M, implying inventory +~$190M), current liabilities rose $174M, so net working capital increased ~$50M. The direct-to-consumer expansion cited for revenue growth entails higher cash operating expenses and inventory investment, which would reduce CFO.

attrs.reason: SG&A rose $201M (E3, E15) with MD&A breakdown: marketing +$41.1M (E39), selling +$63.9M (E40), product innovation/supply chain +$50.7M (E41), corporate services +$45.3M (E42). CFO fell $79.7M (E6, E18) while net income rose; receivables increased $34.5M (E7, E19). The cash outflows for SG&A and receivables build directly explain CFO decline.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The $201M SG&A increase reflects cash outflows for marketing, selling, and supply chain to support DTC expansion, which directly reduces operating cash flow alongside receivables growth.

attrs.reason: Management provided no explicit explanation for the $79.7M decline in operating cash flow despite higher net income. The defender's explanation (higher cash SG&A and inventory investment) is plausible but not management's stated explanation. The numbers show SG&A increased $201M and current assets increased $225M (receivables +$34.5M, implying inventory +~$190M), but the causal link to direct-to-consumer expansion is not explicitly stated in the MD&A.

rebuttal.innocent_explanation: The $79.7M decline in operating cash flow despite higher net income reflects a $201M increase in cash SG&A expenses (marketing +$41M, selling +$64M, product innovation +$51M, corporate +$45M) and a ~$190M increase in inventory and other current assets (current assets rose $225M while receivables rose only $34.5M) to support 18 new retail stores and ecommerce growth, partially offset by a $174M rise in current liabilities.
